> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `master_detail (literal, 49 pages)`
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1af67b26cdf5c6850a4cff8b44a94cf46b7a2502` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c17d8f09197884df29c31bca9bec6f2cecc7db9b` — the merge of head `ad43f0b457457c90866eb2d7418d373ffb9fdfe3` into base `1af67b26cdf5c6850a4cff8b44a94cf46b7a2502`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c17d8f09197884df29c31bca9bec6f2cecc7db9b && git checkout c17d8f09197884df29c31bca9bec6f2cecc7db9b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1af67b26cdf5c6850a4cff8b44a94cf46b7a2502 ad43f0b457457c90866eb2d7418d373ffb9fdfe3 && git checkout -B drift-repro 1af67b26cdf5c6850a4cff8b44a94cf46b7a2502 && git merge --no-ff ad43f0b457457c90866eb2d7418d373ffb9fdfe3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1af67b26cdf5c6850a4cff8b44a94cf46b7a2502
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1af67b26cdf5c6850a4cff8b44a94cf46b7a2502` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

At the door `context.objects` is the registry's served list, with the batch's pending `object_extension` drafts folded in (`runtime-authoring-gate.ts:882-912`, `:1471-1472`). An unmanaged install cannot carry `objectExtensions` (`unmanaged-install.ts:99`), so no install order puts a parent ahead of an extension-added foreign key.

A child write that removes the foreign key is charged; an unrelated edit of a child under a roll-up that was already broken is not (the stored-universe pass).

Every engine reader of `reference` asks the type first: `referenceTargetOf` (`field-value.zod.ts:215-227`), `$expand` (`engine-summaries-and-expansion.ts:910`), the seed loader (`seed-loader.ts:1623`), import (`import-field-meta.ts:103`). So the key links nothing on any other type. The `summary` exemption matches the console's own set (`fieldEnrichment.ts:41-47`). Wrong in two places: see M1 and S1.
- `field/count-named-lookup` (warning): no accept-set change. Right as an advisory; see N1.
- `approval-detail-editable-while-pending` (warning): RIGHT. A node locks unless `lockRecord` is `false` (`lifecycle-hooks.ts:483`), the detail-row lock reads `master_detail` fields only (`:873-886`), and a `lookup` child is a body table only by `relatedList: 'primary'` (`related-list-body-table.ts:93-99`). - `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`: RIGHT. Two publishes that were accepted are refused, and nothing is widened. The PR #36691 record asked for `yes` only because that PR added eleven exports; this one adds none.

### ④ Design judgment

Against card #35143, Data model family only.

**M1 (must-fix) — the console's own field designer writes the shape `field/reference-on-non-reference-type` refuses, and offers no control to repair it.**
- `changeType` in `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/ObjectFieldInspector.tsx:1263-1299` drops `picklist`, option kinds, `referenceNameVisible` and `deleteBehavior` on a retype, each with a comment that the spec refuses the key on the new type. It does not drop `reference`. A field retyped from `lookup` to `text` is saved as text with the old target still on it.
- `writeFields` writes each definition back as it stands (`object-fields-io.ts:45-50`), so nothing else removes the key.
- The Related Object picker is drawn only for `lookup`, `master_detail` and `tree` (`:512-514`, `:1766-1773`). On the retyped field the key is neither shown nor clearable. The way out is to retype back, clear the target and retype again.
- For a Studio author the publish door is the only door (`content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx:474-485`). After this PR that publish is refused, and the stated fix, remove `reference`, names a key the designer does not show. An object that was retyped this way in the past is refused at every later publish, whatever the edit, because the stored self never cancels its own finding.
- The same function already holds the precedent three times (#26729, #29629, #29807): when the spec refuses a type-bound key, the retype removes it, and the #29629 test is titled "so the save is not refused". AGENTS.md Post-Task rule 4 states the principle for removals: the `ui/` fix ships with it, or it does not ship.
- Fix: `changeType` removes `reference` when the next type is none of `lookup`, `master_detail`, `tree`, `user`, `summary`, with a pin in the #29629 shape. For drafts that already hold the key, strip it at the designer's read door or show a control to clear it. This is outside the claim's file surface, so it needs the seat's scope line on this PR, or a `ui/` PR that lands first. M1 closes when the head that lands no longer lets a Studio retype produce the refused shape.

**S1 (should-fix) — the record-picker sentence is wrong for `select` and for every type the inline editor answers before it looks at `reference`.**

Only then does a `reference` send the field to the record picker (`:436-441`). `text`, `number`, `currency`, `percent` and the date types fall through to it, so the sentence is true for those.
- A `select` only parses with options or a picklist, and a picklist's options are served onto the field. So a `select` carrying `reference` is edited with the select widget, and no record id is written into it.
- The sentence is published with `select` named in the entry's `reason` (line 26 of the Scope line's first path) and in the changeset. The rule's message adds it for every type but `formula` and `autonumber` (`data-model-rules.ts:1153-1155`), the docblock names `select` (`:1130`), and the first pin of `data-model-rules.field-reference-shapes.test.ts` asserts `record picker` on a select with options.

**S2 (should-fix) — the relation arm throws where the engine's scan catches, and the throw takes the aggregand refusals with it.**
- `pointsBackTo` reads the carrier through `refOf`, which throws on a `reference` that is not a string. The engine's scan catches exactly that and goes on to the next field (`engine-summaries-and-expansion.ts:303-309`), because one unreadable sibling must not hide a readable foreign key.
- At the door the child is the registry's served object, which can hold such a carrier (a raw registration, or a row stored before the parse tightened; the engine comment names both). The throw leaves `summaryRollupFindings` whole, `runRules` turns it into an `authoring-rule-threw` warning (`runtime-gate.ts:1272-1285`), and the `rollup/non-numeric-aggregand` errors of the same write are lost. Before this PR the entry read no carrier, so that refusal held.
- A parsed stack cannot reach it, so the CLI is unaffected. Fix: catch in `pointsBackTo` and treat the field as not pointing back, as the engine does, with one pin.

Nits, none with an effect on correctness or the contract:
- N1 — `field/count-named-lookup` fires on a lookup named after its target object. The fixture this PR adds does it: `own_total`, a lookup to the `own_total` object. `cycle_count` to a cycle-count object is the same case. Staying silent when the target's name carries the token would cut the noise. Advisory only.
- N2 — The entry comment at `authoring-rules.ts:2602-2606` says the host's stored extensions are folded in at the door. `storedObjectExtensions` is stated on `object_extension` writes only (`runtime-gate.ts:1522`) and this entry's door is `object`, so that read is always empty. The served fields arrive through `context.objects`. The result is right; the comment is not.
- N3 — The entry's `reason`, the changeset and the docblock say the summary is "never indexed". That holds for the first arm. With a `relationshipField` that names no child field the summary is indexed and never recomputed. Same outcome for the author. It can ride the S1 edit.
- N4 — R8's `refOf(def)` arm (`data-model-rules.ts:1316`) and its two undeclared keys, from section ③. A follow-up card.
- N5 — The four new rule ids are module-local, while the file's other ids are exported constants (#22161), and none has an `os explain` entry. The tests retype the slugs. Accepted as the price of `Clause-②: no`; export them when a consumer needs to compare ids.
